objetivo: Explicar qué es el inglés marítimo y por qué la OMI exige su uso a bordo.

parrafos: English is the {{working language}} of the sea. A ship can have a {{crew}} from five or six different countries. The captain may be Greek, the engineers Filipino and the cadets Mexican. To work safely together, everybody on board needs one common language.

Maritime English is the English used at sea and in ports. It is not the same as everyday English. It has special words for the parts of the ship, for navigation and for the engine room, and it uses short, clear sentences.

On the {{bridge}}, the {{officer of the watch}} talks by VHF radio with other ships, with a {{coast station}} and with {{VTS}} centres. A {{misunderstanding}} on the radio can cause a collision or a grounding.

For this reason, the IMO adopted the {{SMCP}} in 2001. SMCP means Standard Marine Communication Phrases. These {{standard phrases}} have only one meaning, so every seafarer understands them in the same way. The STCW Convention requires deck officers to understand and use them.

VTS.es: Servicio de Tráfico Marítimo (Vessel Traffic Service)

SMCP.es: Frases Normalizadas de la OMI para las Comunicaciones Marítimas

ejercicios.enunciado: Why do ships need one common language?
opciones: Because crews come from different countries
Because English is an easy language
Because ships only sail to English-speaking ports
